solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Well-to-do duke, American

parts.note: Prospero is the deposed Duke of Milan in Shakespeare's The Tempest

explanation.surface: A wealthy American aristocrat is described in a terse society-column note.
explanation.walkthrough: The duke is a particular one: Prospero, the magician hero of The Tempest, once Duke of Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone wealthy and doing well financially; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Go to check king's ready

indicators.note: to check is to hold back or contain, so the energy word holds the king's letter

parts.note: go means energy or vigour, which is pep
R stands for rex, Latin for king; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look in on the king and see whether he is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is the noun meaning energy, not the verb, and 'check' means restrain or hold in, not inspect.
explanation.definitionFit: To ready something is to get it prepared, and prep is informal shorthand for prepare.

clue.text: The setter's leaving nothing of importance working

indicators.note: the setter's letters leave the importance word and the nothing letter takes their place

parts.note: something imperative is vitally important
the setter's is the setter saying 'I am', shortened to I'M
O is the zero shape standing for nothing

explanation.surface: The compiler steps away from anything that matters while still on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The setter's' is the setter speaking: I'm. 'Nothing' then takes its place at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine or law that is operative is functioning or in force, the same as in working order.

clue.text: Religious leader in huff about being elevated

parts.note: to be in a pet is to be in a huff, a fit of sulking

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word means writing it bottom to top, so about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A cleric sulks over being promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated' reads like promotion in the church, but in a down entry it means the letters are written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Peter, the apostle, is regarded as the first leader of the Christian church.

clue.text: Salesperson with additional pay for extra performance

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a rise is an increase in salary

explanation.surface: A sales rep gets a bonus for working overtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprise is a repeated performance of a piece, an encore or repeat showing.

clue.text: Incompetent being this would make fuse start to fail

parts.words: being this would make fuse start to fail
parts.note: read the entry as two words, 'use' and 'less': the word fuse made less its first letter, F, leaves use, so fuse's start has failed

explanation.surface: A useless electrician complains that a fuse keeps blowing.
explanation.walkthrough: The entry split in two says 'use, less': fuse less its start, F, is use. That is how being this makes the start of fuse fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone useless at a task is inept and lacking skill, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Retailer sells hopeless clothes

indicators.note: to clothe is to cover, so the phrase sells hopeless wraps round the word inside it

explanation.surface: A shop sells clothes that nobody wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like the noun for garments; it is the verb, meaning the outer words dress the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer is a business selling to the public, which is what a store is.

clue.text: Evil alter ego contracted artist … monster!

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the last letter of the alter ego is dropped

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the evil other self of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's novella
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter is taken over by his villainous second self and becomes a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hydra is the many-headed serpent of Greek myth that Hercules fought, a classic monster.

clue.text: Siren in temple curtailed exercise

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail cut off, so the temple loses its last letter

parts.note: the Parthenon is the temple of Athena on the Acropolis in Athens
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A seductive woman shows up at the temple for a shortened workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siren' sounds modern, but it is one of the Sirens of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Parthenope was one of the Sirens of Greek legend, and Naples was built where her body washed ashore.

clue.text: Progress to pull a good pint

definitions.meaning: to progress is to advance or succeed in life
a well-pulled pint of beer gets a foam head on it

explanation.walkthrough: Read as three words, the phrase also means giving a beer its foam top, which a barman pulling a good pint does.
explanation.definitionFit: To get on in a career is to advance, and a good pint gets a frothy top.

clue.text: Employ most of dinosaurs in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the shortened word is read backwards
most of means all but the last letter

parts.note: T. rexes are tyrannosaurs, the best-known dinosaurs

explanation.surface: Someone takes on most of the dinosaurs from a retired collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' drops the last S to leave TREXE; 'in retirement' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert strength or influence is to employ it, bringing it to bear.

clue.text: One acts like eight or nine of French Resistance

parts.note: eight or nine o'clock comes before ten, so it is pre-ten
de is French for of
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone fakes membership of the French Resistance, as eight or nine people did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eight or nine' are numbers below ten, so 'like' them is pre-ten. 'French Resistance' looks like one wartime name, but splits into 'of French' (DE) and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender puts on an act, claiming to be something or someone that he is not.

clue.text: Very fine hour with fliers

parts.note: an airline is a company that flies people

explanation.surface: An airline's timekeeping is complimented as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very fine' sounds like praise, but it means extremely thin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline crack or line is extremely thin, as thin as a single hair.

clue.text: Cause embarrassment to party that's after answer

indicators.note: after says the party word follows the answer letter

parts.note: a bash is an informal party

explanation.surface: A party held after the answer is known proves embarrassing.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash someone is to make them ashamed or disconcerted.

clue.text: Not working having left monastery

definitions.meaning: a machine that has broken down is broken, unusable
a monk who quits leaves his religious order, and so is out of it

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: a monastery's community is a religious order, and leaving it puts you outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken lift is out of service; a monk who has left is outside his religious community.

clue.text: Use just over half of gas etc supplied by London area

indicators.note: supplied by says the London district comes after the utility part
five of the nine letters is just over half, so the last four go

parts.note: gas, water and electricity are utilities
SE is the south-east postal district of London

explanation.surface: Use a little more than half of the gas a London district supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: To utilise something is to make use of it; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Traitor's doing well with Queen

parts.note: a sportsman doing well is in form
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A spy is thriving with royal favour.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Traitor is 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An informer betrays people to the authorities, a kind of traitor or grass.

clue.text: Sugar-coat reports circulating about alien base

indicators.note: about means around, so the reversed reports go round the alien and base
circulating means going round, so the reports word is read backwards

parts.note: news is reports of events
ET is the extraterrestrial of Spielberg's film
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: News of an alien base is spun to make it palatable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulating' reads the reports backwards as SWEN, and 'about' wraps that round ETE. The base is e, the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: To sugar-coat bad news is to make it more agreeable, as sweetening makes food pleasanter.

clue.text: Universal bar suits regularly getting promoted over Fast and Furious

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the reversed part sits above the fast word
in a down clue promotion moves letters upward, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: U is the film classification for universal

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of bar suits

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Universal Studios promotes the Fast and Furious film franchise.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of 'bar suits' are BRUT, so U plus BRUT reversed gives TURBU. Universal and Fast & Furious suggest the film studio and franchise.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent weather or water is wild and violent, as something furious is.

clue.text: Stuffed on account of agent

parts.note: to fall out over something is to fall out because of it
a fed is an FBI agent

explanation.surface: An agent is filled up on expenses.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stuffed has eaten too much, which is to be overfed.

clue.text: American airport terminal's beginning to be most boring

parts.note: Dulles is the international airport serving Washington DC

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of the word terminal

explanation.surface: An American airport terminal is judged the dullest place to wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Dullest is the superlative of dull, meaning the most tedious or uninteresting.

clue.text: Disappointing holiday, a possible result of taking drugs?

definitions.meaning: a holiday that goes wrong is a poor journey

definitions.text: a possible result of taking drugs?
definitions.meaning: a frightening hallucinogenic experience is called this

explanation.definitionFit: A poor journey is literally a bad outing, and the slang term means a nightmarish drug experience.

clue.text: Holding up trophies, substitute's where coach might be

indicators.note: in a down clue holding up means raising, so the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: pots are trophies won in sport
a sub is a substitute; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A substitute holds up the trophies where the team coach might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like the team's trainer; it is the bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach, meaning a long-distance bus, waits at a stop for passengers.

clue.text: Stranger died in European river

indicators.note: in places the died letter inside the river

parts.note: the Oder flows along the German-Polish border

explanation.surface: A stranger died in a European river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun for an unknown person; it is the comparative of strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stranger is more peculiar or odd than another.

clue.text: Duck crackers

definitions.meaning: the Warner Bros cartoon duck bears this name

explanation.definitionFit: The Looney Tunes cartoon duck is named for being slightly mad, which is also what crackers means.

clue.text: Need discovered French author to be bright

parts.note: lust is a strong craving or need

indicators.note: discovered means with its cover taken off, so the author loses his outer letters

parts.note: Marcel Proust wrote In Search of Lost Time

explanation.surface: A French author needs to be found in order to shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' looks like found, but means uncovered: Proust loses his first and last letters to leave ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lustrous is shining or glossy, giving off a bright sheen.

clue.text: Performing song with this religious leader could be absorbing

indicators.note: performing means putting through actions, so the letters of song and the answer are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A rabbi sings a song and finds it gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing' rearranges SONG plus this answer to make ABSORBING, so the answer is ABSORBING less SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish teacher and the leader of a synagogue's congregation.

clue.text: One's one to have one on the Walk of Fame

definitions.text: One's one to have one on the Walk of Fame

parts.words: One's one to have one on the Walk of Fame
parts.note: a celebrity is honoured on the Hollywood Walk of Fame with a five-pointed plaque in the pavement, called by the same word

explanation.walkthrough: The Hollywood Walk of Fame is a pavement set with five-pointed plaques for celebrities, so a famous person gets one named the same as themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrity is called by the same word as the five-pointed emblem set into the Hollywood pavement for each one.

clue.text: Unusual gear? Just three-quarters of it

indicators.note: nine of the gear word's twelve letters is three-quarters, so the last three go

parts.note: the differential is the gear in a car's axle letting wheels turn at ... speeds

explanation.surface: Someone queries an unusual gear that only has three-quarters of its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlike others is not the usual kind, so the words are near-synonyms.

clue.text: British remain in port

parts.note: the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: A British voter wants to stay in at a port, echoing Brexit.
explanation.definitionFit: Brest is a naval port in Brittany, north-west France.

clue.text: Lift articulated beams

indicators.note: articulated means spoken, so the lift word is to be heard

parts.note: to lift something is to raise it

explanation.surface: An articulated lift is held up by beams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articulated' suggests a jointed lorry or crane; it means pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: Beams of light are shafts or rays shining from a source.

clue.text: Priest sets out to find relative

indicators.note: out means put out of place, so the letters of priest sets are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A priest sets out to find a long-lost relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepsister is a step-parent's daughter, a family member by marriage.
